**Test image observations:** A single elongated mango leaf, mostly dried/withered. One half shows a deep black coating/encrustation covering the leaf surface, while the other half is tan/brown (dried). The black material appears superficial and coating-like rather than sunken lesions.

**Key evidence:**
- Extensive black surface coating on the leaf — characteristic of sooty mould fungal growth on honeydew deposits
- The coating appears superficial (not sunken/raised lesions), matching sooty mould description
- Sooty mould reference images show similar dark black patches/encrustation on mango leaves

This clearly distinguishes from Anthracnose (sunken dark lesions), Bacterial Canker (raised angular spots with halos), or Powdery Mildew (white powdery growth).
